title: views.json
description: The extra panels a project adds to its dashboard, in .human-in-the-lead/views.json beside tracker.json (decisions HITLD-684, 685 and 687). A panel is data only: a named filter over the fields of the dashboard data contract (schemas/dashboard-data.schema.json), and one panel type from a closed set (table, board, bar, line, timeline, graph). No key names code to run, and nothing in the file is drawn as markup: every value is shown as text. A field is named as the contract's item names it (id, kind, title, state, stage, project, needs, open_needs, created, critical, waiting_on_it, decider, waiting_on, scopes, classification, owner, redacted), as reached.<state> (the date an item first reached that state, from the committed state history), or as a field tracker.json declares, by its name or as fields.<name> (a bare name is the contract's own first). hitld check views and hitld dashboard refuse a panel that names a field or a value that does not exist, naming the field and the panel. The project's panels show in their own tab, named by title; the built-in views do not change.

title.description: The name of the project's tab on the dashboard.

panels.description: The panels, in the order they show.

field.description: A field of the contract's items, reached.<state>, or a declared field (by name or as fields.<name>).

scalar.description: A value to compare with: text, a number or true or false. A date is text, YYYY-MM-DD.

filter.description: One condition on a field; a panel shows the items that meet every one. Give the field and exactly one test. On a field that holds a list, is means the list holds the value, in that it holds any of them, and set that it is not empty. at_least and at_most compare numbers, and dates as YYYY-MM-DD text.

set.description: true: the item has a value (a list that is not empty); false: it has none.

panel.description: One panel. Which keys apply depends on type: table takes columns (and sort, order, limit); board takes group_by (and limit); bar takes group_by; line takes date (and interval, cumulative); timeline takes date (and end, limit); graph takes relation (default needs). A key the type does not take is refused.

id.description: The panel's name in the file and on the page: lower case, digits and hyphens. Unique in the file.

type.description: The panel type, from the closed set (decision HITLD-685).

where.description: The conditions an item meets to be in the panel; none means every work, decision and external item.

columns.description: table: the fields shown, in order. The item's ID always comes first.

sort.description: table: the field the rows are ordered by. Default: the ID.

group_by.description: board: the field whose values are the columns; bar: the field whose values are counted. An item whose field holds a list counts under each value.

date.description: line: the date counted over time; timeline: the date an item is placed at. created, reached.<state>, or a declared text field that holds YYYY-MM-DD dates.

end.description: timeline: a second date where an item's span ends.

interval.description: line: how the dates are counted. Default: week (weeks start on Monday).

cumulative.description: line: count every item up to each date, not only those in it.

relation.description: graph: the field that links an item to the items it waits on: needs (default), open_needs, or a declared list field that holds IDs.

limit.description: table, board and timeline: the most items shown; the panel says how many more there are. Default 200.
